family.description_more: Read the rest of the description
family.no_headline: The atlas found no headline statement in this paper’s TeX source.
family.readings_heading: Does the Lean state the whole theorem?
family.readings_intro: Two [[readers|outside readers]] compared this family’s Lean statements with its headline. Each verdict below is theirs, in their own term, with their note.
family.withdrawn_intro: These papers were listed under this family when the release was published (CONTENTS.md at its first commit), when it was titled “{title}”. OpenAI has since withdrawn them; each notice is quoted below.
family.finite_heading: Finite parts checked by exact computation
family.finite_intro: Carlos Toledo’s cert-machine decides finite parts of papers with [[exact-check|exact code]] written independently from each paper, reading the release’s files at the pinned commit. Each check says whether it decides the whole headline or one finite component of an argument whose other parts it does not decide.

finite_words.needs-data: Needs data that was not published

family.finite_detail: What was decided, in cert-machine’s words
family.hol_intro: Ben Knill proved selected steps of this family again in [[hol-light|HOL Light]], independently of Lean, with negative controls that must fail. The author states that no card proves a headline theorem of the release. Quoted under CC BY 4.0.
family.lean_scope_source: From the release’s Lean notes for this family
family.citations_heading: What it cites, and what cites it
family.citations_intro: These links come from the papers’ bibliographies. A citation records that one paper cites another; how each cited result is used has not been examined here.
family.cites_none: Its papers cite no other paper in the release.
family.cited_none: No other paper in the release cites it.
family.refs_intro: Outside works the papers cite, with where in each paper the citation appears.
family.superseded: This is an earlier edition. The current edition is {link}.
family.explain_heading: Explain a result, compare statements or propose a correction
family.explain_none: Atlas has no contributed explanation for this family yet. You can offer one with a GitHub account. You receive named credit and disclose any AI assistance.
family.explain_progress_intro: These drafts are recorded in Atlas’s repository with no reviewer approval recorded.
family.check_button: Compare the Lean statement with the paper
family.check_choose: Check a statement: choose one of {n}
family.check_choose_intro: Each statement is checked on its own. Choose the one you have read:
family.contribute_intro: Each button opens a GitHub form with this page and its source version filled in. Opening the form does not reserve the work.
family.xref_title: A cross-reference to {label} in the paper
family.method_notes: OpenAI’s method notes for this family
family.reasoning_summary: OpenAI released an abridged summary of the model’s reasoning for this family:
family.formulations_heading: Other mathematical statements in OpenAI’s Lean library
family.formulations_intro: Atlas found these propositions by scanning the text of the project’s Model.lean file. Each name links to its definition, with any associated statement file beside it. This list does not record running Lean to interpret or verify those definitions.
family.formulations_more: {n} more formulations are in the same file.
family.formulations_theorems: The source scan also found {n} theorem or lemma declarations whose names contain ‘manuscript’.
family.facts_lean_none: no Lean statement in the release
family.facts_withdrawn_1: One more paper was withdrawn after the release.
family.facts_withdrawn_n: {n} more papers were withdrawn after the release.
family.facts_problems_1: One report of a problem from an outside reader.
family.facts_problems_n: {n} reports of problems from outside readers.
family.facts_erdos: It bears on {problems}, as listed by {source}.
family.bench_heading: The theorem and its Lean statement
family.no_headline_any: The atlas found no headline statement in this family’s papers. They are listed below.
family.lean_main: in OpenAI’s list of main results
family.lean_support: outside OpenAI’s list of main results
family.lean_note: A [[challenge|Lean statement]] states the theorem and leaves its proof as [[sorry|`sorry`]]. [[comparator|Comparator]] checks OpenAI’s proof against it.
family.lean_note_axiom: A [[challenge|Lean statement]] states the theorem; this one writes `axiom mainStatement` where others write [[sorry|`sorry`]]. [[comparator|Comparator]] checks OpenAI’s proof against it.
family.runs_note: Each is that group’s own report. The atlas has not repeated the runs.
family.runs_none: No outside group has reported re-running it yet.

run_verdict.built: built the solution; Comparator not run

family.thread_label: The thread: a candidate pairing of {theorem} with the Lean statement {label}
family.nothread_weak: No thread is drawn. Too few words are shared to pick out which theorem this Lean statement states, so the paper’s first headline theorem is shown.
family.nothread_tie: No thread is drawn. Two theorems matched this Lean statement equally well, so the paper’s first headline theorem is shown.
family.nothread_none: No thread is drawn. The atlas found no extracted statement in the papers this Lean statement names.
family.nolean_text: The release has no Lean statement for this family, so the paper is its only record.
family.nolean_invite: Formalising it is open work. If you write a Lean statement of this theorem, share it through
family.draft_scope: The atlas also holds a draft reading of OpenAI’s Lean note by an AI agent, which nobody has reviewed: it classes this Lean statement as one that {label}.

reading_v.narrower-declared: States less, and OpenAI’s note says so
reading_v.narrower-undeclared: States less, and OpenAI’s note does not say so
reading_v.narrower-unlinked: States less; the rest is in a paper the note does not link

family.note_heading: OpenAI’s own note on what its Lean covers
family.note_rest: Read the rest of the note
family.index_why_none: no extracted statement in its papers
family.index_rest: {n} more headline statements, none with a Lean statement, are
family.checks_heading: What has been checked, and what is left to check
family.checks_intro: Every check here is credited to whoever ran it. The atlas shows their reports and has not repeated them.
family.rt_intro: Each cell is one group’s [[rerun|re-run]] of one Lean statement, linked to their record.
family.left_nolean: Everything formal: the release has no Lean statement for this family.
family.left_pairing_1: Whether the pairing is right. It was found by shared words, and nobody has reviewed it.
family.left_pairing_n: Whether each of the {n} [[pairing|pairings]] is right. They were found by shared words, and nobody has reviewed them.
family.left_holes_1: Comparator compares one definition by name and type only, so what it means must be read. See [[holes|definition holes]].
family.left_holes_n: Comparator compares {n} definitions by name and type only, so what they mean must be read. See [[holes|definition holes]].
family.left_scope: The draft scope classifications, made by an AI agent from OpenAI’s notes. Nobody has reviewed them.
family.left_finite_1: One finite part that the exact computation did not decide. That says nothing against the result.
family.left_finite_n: {n} finite parts that the exact computation did not decide. That says nothing against the result.
family.left_data_1: One finite part that needs data the release did not publish.
family.left_data_n: {n} finite parts that need data the release did not publish.
family.finite_undecided_note: An undecided check says nothing against the result.
family.papers_intro: Each paper opens as a [[reading-page|reading page]] in the browser, with the PDF beside it. The statements each paper opens with are folded under it.
family.paper_fold: Abstract and the {n} statements it opens with
family.index_heading_nolean: Other theorems the papers open with
family.runs_how: How each group ran it, in their words
family.draft_scope_unclear: The atlas also holds a draft reading of OpenAI’s Lean note by an AI agent, which nobody has reviewed: it finds the note unclear about this Lean statement.
family.draft_scope_none: No draft reading of OpenAI’s Lean note classifies this Lean statement yet.
family.tier_said: An unsigned public tier list, the {name}, classes it as a {type} and rates its significance, if it holds up, as “{tier}”. The page says that nothing on it is verified.
family.thread_one: The dashed thread marks a candidate [[pairing|pairing]] of {theorem} with this Lean statement.
family.thread_many: The atlas pairs {theorem} with {n} Lean statements: {shown}, shown here; {others}.
family.thread_words_both: It found the pairing by words the theorem shares with the Lean statement’s title and names ({lean}) and with OpenAI’s Lean note for this family ({note}).
family.thread_words_lean: It found the pairing by words the theorem shares with the Lean statement’s title and names ({lean}).
family.thread_words_note: It found the pairing by words the theorem shares with OpenAI’s Lean note for this family ({note}), quoted below.
family.lean_more_1: And one more theorem in this file:
family.lean_more_n: And {n} more theorems in this file:
family.support_subnote: The release’s Lean is paired with this theorem, not with the headline above. The outside readers’ verdicts are below.
family.support_claim_note: The headline theorem of the first paper OpenAI lists for this family, as that paper states it. No Lean statement in the release is paired with it.
family.bench_heading_support: The theorem, and what the release’s Lean states
family.paper_fold_1: Abstract and the statement it opens with
family.refs_none_in: The atlas found no outside references in {title}.
family.facts_tier: The {source} records it as a {type}, and rates its significance, if it holds up, as “{tier}”.
family.disagree_lead: The two readings disagree: {a} reads the Lean as stating {ga}, and {b} as stating {gb}.
family.thread_caption: The dashed thread marks a candidate [[pairing|pairing]]. The atlas matched {theorem} to this Lean statement by the words they share ({words}). Nobody has reviewed it.

agree.agree-full: Both find it stated in full.
agree.agree-less: Both find that the Lean states less.
agree.disagree: Their readings differ, and both stand.

family.index_same: Also paired with the theorem above: {items}.

explanation.reviewed_note: Recorded in the atlas as reviewed. The reviewer and the scope of the review are listed below.
explanation.version: Release version it was written against
explanation.older_version: An earlier version of the release than this atlas shows.
explanation.description: An explanation of part or all of family {id} in OpenAI’s mathematics release: {title}.

statement.claim_lean_intro: The lines of the Lean statement that state the theorem, then the definitions in the file that it uses.
statement.note_heading: OpenAI’s own note on what this Lean statement covers
statement.draft_line: An AI agent drafted an interpretation of that note, classifying this statement as “{cls}”. No human review of the draft is recorded.
statement.defs_intro: Local definitions the statement names, followed through the definitions they name in turn. The match is by name in the source text, so a name reached only through notation can be missed; the full file is below.
statement.defs_more: {n} more definitions are reached the same way; the full file lists them.
statement.sorry_note: A [[challenge|Lean statement]] states the theorem and leaves its proof as [[sorry|`sorry`]] on purpose. OpenAI’s proof is in a separate solution module, and a program called Comparator checks that proof against this statement.
statement.sorry_note_axiom: A [[challenge|Lean statement]] states the theorem and leaves its proof open. This file writes `axiom mainStatement` where others write `sorry`; OpenAI’s solution module proves `main` directly, and a program called Comparator checks that proof against this statement.
statement.main_yes: OpenAI lists this as a main result in its Lean catalogue.
statement.main_no: OpenAI’s Lean catalogue does not list this as a main result; the release’s Lean notes for family {id} link it.
statement.permitted_axioms_note: The axioms this configuration allows a proof to use. A replay shows which of them a proof uses.
statement.lines: Lines of Lean, without comments or blank lines
statement.axiom_heading: A note on how this file states its claim
statement.axiom_note: Line {line} of this statement file writes `axiom mainStatement : MainClaim` where other statement files write `sorry`. It stands in for the proof on the statement side only. OpenAI’s solution proves `main` directly, in {solution_link}. A successful Comparator replay checks the solution against the allowed axioms: {axioms}.
statement.paper_heading: Every extracted statement of the accompanying papers
statement.paper_intro: The statements the atlas extracted automatically from each accompanying paper’s TeX source, with links to the full sources.
statement.card_intro: A shareable summary of this page: the proposed paper match, what the Lean statement expresses, and which reviews are recorded.
statement.card_vocab_pure: Imports only Mathlib; no local vocabulary added
statement.reruns_intro: These groups report running [[comparator|Comparator]] for this statement file. Depending on its settings, Comparator verifies a proof or compares definitions by name and type. Each report is credited and quoted in the group’s own terms. Atlas has not repeated the runs.
statement.reasons_heading: Questions to resolve when comparing this statement with the paper
statement.check_button: Compare this statement with the paper
statement.checks_none: Atlas records no contributed comparison of this statement with the paper.
statement.replays_none: Atlas records no contributed report of running Comparator for this statement file.
statement.og_alt: Statement comparison for {label}: a candidate paper statement beside the Lean statement, with its scope and review status.
statement.holes_intro: Comparator checks only the name and type of each definition listed here. The body a proof is checked against is the definition in OpenAI’s solution library, so a reader must read it there as well as in this file.
statement.hole_item: Comparator checks the name and type of `{name}`; its definition is in OpenAI’s library at {link}.
statement.hole_item_nolink: Comparator checks the name and type of `{name}`; its definition is in OpenAI’s library, in the modules that `{module}` imports.
statement.card_holes_one: Comparator checks only the name and type of `{name}`; its body comes from the solution.
statement.card_holes_many: Comparator checks only the name and type of {n} definitions, among them `{name}`; their bodies come from the solution.
statement.coverage_source: OpenAI’s Lean note for this family
statement.coverage_stale: This AI-drafted interpretation describes a different release version, so it is not shown.
statement.comparator_box_heading: What an accepted Comparator run would establish
statement.comparator_box_does: If [[comparator|Comparator]] is run under this configuration and accepts, the solution proves the configured theorem using only the [[axioms|allowed axioms]], and the [[kernel|Lean kernel]] accepts every step.
statement.comparator_box_holes: This configuration lists {n} [[holes|definition holes]]: {names}. Comparator compares these by name and type only; their bodies come from the solution.
statement.comparator_box_noholes: This configuration lists no definition holes, so every definition the statement uses is compared as it is written in this file.
statement.comparator_box_not: Acceptance leaves open whether the Lean statement means the same thing as the paper’s theorem, whether the paper’s other claims are correct, and whether the result is new. Those questions require comparing the definitions and statements, reviewing the paper’s arguments, and reading the earlier literature.

paper.in_result_withdrawn: Listed under family {id}, then titled “{title}”, when the release was published; OpenAI has since withdrawn it.
paper.see_result_now: See the family as it stands

explain.title: Families
explain.lede: OpenAI groups related papers into {families} families. Each row links to the papers, their Lean statements and independent assessments.
explain.readers_note: MathVet and cert-machine assessed whether each family’s Lean statements express the whole result OpenAI describes in its catalogue. Each column gives Atlas’s description first, followed by the group’s own term in quotation marks.
explain.caption: Every family in the release, one per row, in the release’s order.
explain.problems_1: One problem reported, not judged by the atlas
explain.problems_n: {n} problems reported, not judged by the atlas
explain.ev_ring: Has another proof or calculation report
explain.invite: {open} of {families} families have no explanation written for the atlas yet. An explanation for mathematicians outside a family’s area is one of the most useful things to add, and each family page has a button to offer one.
explain.invite_all: No family has an explanation written for the atlas yet. An explanation for mathematicians outside a family’s area is one of the most useful things to add, and each family page has a button to offer one.
explain.how: The contributing guide sets out what to include and how the work is reviewed.
explain.queue_heading: Where a careful reading is most useful
explain.queue_intro: The first {n} of the {flagged} Lean statements with a specific reason for a careful reading, each with its reasons.
explain.queue_not_verdict: The order allocates reading time and says nothing about whether any statement or proof is correct.
explain.counts_note: Menu counts are for the whole release.
explain.cited_link: The papers cited most within the release are listed on their own page.

statements.title: Lean statements
statements.lede: Lean is a language for mathematical statements and proofs that a computer can verify. The release supplies {lean} statement files for the Comparator proof-verification program. OpenAI’s Lean catalogue lists {main} as main results. Sort the list by any column.
statements.filter: Filter by name, family or discipline

numbers.title: Numbers
numbers.lede: Every number the atlas states in a sentence, with what it counts, the rule that counts it, whether it was computed or reported, and who it is credited to. Each one opens the records behind it.
numbers.states_note: Statement Map, the program that collects Atlas’s source records, computes each number and saves the items counted. A total supplied only by a source is marked as reported. If inputs are missing, the page says so instead of displaying zero.
numbers.credit_common: Unless a number names its own credit, its records are credited to: {credit}
numbers.records_nojs: The complete list of counted items and their sources is available as JSON, a machine-readable text format:
numbers.two_inventories: Atlas retains two lists of citations between papers. Statement Map’s current extraction finds {current} ordered pairs of citing and cited papers. Atlas’s earlier extraction finds {baseline}; it lacks the additional pairs found by Statement Map. Neither list is claimed to contain every citation.

state.reported: Reported by the source; its members are not listed.
state.incomplete: Incomplete: some inputs are missing, so only the known part is shown.

group.scope: AI-drafted assessments of what the Lean statements express
group.papers: Numbered statement types in the papers’ source files

group_intro.scope: An AI agent classified OpenAI’s note about what each Lean statement expresses. No human review of these classifications is recorded, so these counts describe drafts.
group_intro.library: Counts obtained by scanning the text of OpenAI’s Lean library at the source version shown here. Lean was not run to interpret or verify the files for these counts.
group_intro.papers: Counts of TeX blocks labelled as theorems, lemmas, definitions and other statement types, added across the current papers. These are source labels, not assessments that the statements are correct.
group_intro.community: Reports by people and groups outside OpenAI. A finding is a report, not a judgement by the atlas.

js.failed: The records could not load. Open the linked source file above.
js.generation: The records and this page were built from different versions of the source data, so the records are not shown.
js.none_listed: The source reports this total without listing its members.
js.digest: SHA-256 identifier for these source records: {sha}

labels.atlas_baseline_manuscripts_citing_unform: papers citing a paper without associated Lean, in the Atlas baseline inventory

labels.community_people: people and groups credited for them

labels.model_statement_projects_linked_to_a_fam: projects with Model.lean statements linked to a family

numbers.upstream_formalised_atlas: The atlas counts {n} current papers listed as accompanying papers in family notes that link a Lean statement, whatever part of the paper that Lean statement covers. OpenAI’s figure counts formalised headline results.
numbers.upstream_intro: OpenAI’s reported figures and the atlas’s related counts, with the measure and source for each.
numbers.withdrawn_intro: The release withdrew {n} papers. Their notices are quoted in full.
numbers.changelog_source: Quoted from the release’s history file

rule_words.families: Each family number in OpenAI’s catalogue, counted once.
rule_words.disciplines: Each discipline the catalogue groups families under, in the catalogue’s order and with its names.
rule_words.manuscripts_current: Each paper the release lists as current.
rule_words.manuscripts_withdrawn: Each paper the release lists as withdrawn.
rule_words.manuscripts_previous_editions: Each paper the release lists as an earlier edition of a later paper.
rule_words.statements_lean: Each Lean statement with its configuration. One Lean statement may name several theorems.
rule_words.statements_lean_main_results: Each Lean statement that names at least one theorem the release lists as a main result.
rule_words.main_result_declarations: Each main result the release lists, counted once per entry, even when two entries share a name.
rule_words.distinct_target_theorems: Each theorem a configuration names, counted once for each pair of solution file and theorem name. Every configuration that names it is kept in the records.
rule_words.families_with_lean: Each family whose Lean scope note in the release links at least one Lean statement. A link says the two are associated; it does not say how much of the family’s claim the Lean states.
rule_words.manuscripts_with_lean: Each current paper that a Lean scope note in the release names as an accompanying paper, whatever part of the paper the Lean covers.
rule_words.lean_definition_holes: Each definition a configuration leaves for the solution to supply, counted once per configuration, repeats included. These are what a configuration lists; they say nothing about what a proof actually uses.
rule_words.lean_statements_pure_mathlib: Each Lean statement whose text defines no local vocabulary and imports nothing from outside Mathlib.
rule_words.lean_statements_no_local_vocabulary: Each Lean statement whose text defines no local vocabulary.
rule_words.lean_statements_with_custom_vocabulary: Each Lean statement whose text defines at least one piece of local vocabulary.
rule_words.lean_statements_importing_non_mathlib: Each Lean statement that imports at least one file from outside Mathlib.
rule_words.lean_statements_declaring_axioms: Each Lean statement whose text declares an axiom. This reads the text; it does not trace what a proof depends on.
rule_words.lean_vocabulary_total: Each local definition found by reading the text of the Lean statements, leaving out the theorems and lemmas themselves. Lean did not elaborate these files for this count.
rule_words.lean_vocabulary_median: The median number of local definitions per Lean statement, counting statements with none. With an even number of statements it is the average of the two middle values.
rule_words.lean_vocabulary_max: The largest number of local definitions in one Lean statement. The records list every statement that reaches it.
rule_words.internal_citation_edges: Each pair of papers in which one cites the other, counted once in each direction. A citation records that one paper cites another; it says nothing about how the cited result is used.
rule_words.atlas_baseline_internal_citation_edges: Each pair of papers in which one cites the other, counted once in each direction, from the atlas’s own earlier extraction. A citation records that one paper cites another; it says nothing about how the cited result is used.
rule_words.manuscripts_citing_collection: Each current paper that cites at least one other paper in the release.
rule_words.atlas_baseline_manuscripts_citing_collec: Each current paper that cites at least one other paper in the release, from the atlas’s own earlier extraction.
rule_words.manuscripts_citing_unformalised_collecti: Each current paper that cites a paper in the release with no associated Lean statement, or the latest edition of one. Having no associated Lean says nothing about whether the result could be formalised.
rule_words.atlas_baseline_manuscripts_citing_unform: The same count from the atlas’s own earlier extraction: each current paper that cites a paper in the release with no associated Lean statement, or the latest edition of one.
rule_words.external_citations: Each reference key in a current paper’s bibliography that points outside the release, counted once per paper and key. Two keys grouped as the same work still count twice.
rule_words.external_works_cited: Each work outside the release cited by current papers, grouped automatically by DOI, then arXiv identifier, then title. No manual review of the grouping is recorded.
rule_words.community_efforts: Each independent project or body of work credited by Atlas. Recording a reported problem does not establish that the report is correct.
rule_words.community_findings: Each report from those projects or bodies of work credited by Atlas. Recording a reported problem does not establish that the report is correct.
rule_words.community_people: Each distinct name or handle credited across those efforts, as written. The atlas has not confirmed who is behind each name.
rule_words.lean_files: The number of Lean files in OpenAI’s library, as the release reports it.
rule_words.lean_projects: Each project folder in OpenAI’s Lean library that holds Lean files.
rule_words.projects_with_model_file: Each project in OpenAI’s Lean library with at least one file named Model.lean. The next number counts the files.
rule_words.model_files: The number of Model.lean files in OpenAI’s library, as the release reports it.
rule_words.model_statement_definitions: Each definition of a proposition in a Model.lean file, found by reading the text. Lean did not build these files for this count.
rule_words.model_statement_projects_linked_to_a_fam: Each project whose Model.lean statements are linked to a family. This says nothing about the library’s other projects.
rule_words.manuscript_theorems: Each theorem or lemma in OpenAI’s library whose name contains the word ‘manuscript’, found by reading the text. Lean did not build these files for this count.
rule_words.projects_with_manuscript_theorems: Each project that holds one of those theorems. This says nothing about the library’s other projects.
rule_words.manuscript_theorems_checked_by_comparato: Each of those theorems whose name is exactly the theorem a configuration names. A matching name says nothing about how much of the paper is proved.
rule_words.scope_statements_classified: Each Lean statement given a draft classification by an AI agent. The classifications have no recorded human review and do not establish that a Lean statement means the same thing as the paper.
rule_words.paper_environments_theorem: The number of theorem environments in the TeX source of each current paper, added up over the papers. These are counted separately from the statements the atlas lists for each paper.
rule_words.paper_environments_lemma: The number of lemma environments in the TeX source of each current paper, added up over the papers. These are counted separately from the statements the atlas lists for each paper.
rule_words.paper_environments_proposition: The number of proposition environments in the TeX source of each current paper, added up over the papers. These are counted separately from the statements the atlas lists for each paper.
rule_words.paper_environments_corollary: The number of corollary environments in the TeX source of each current paper, added up over the papers. These are counted separately from the statements the atlas lists for each paper.
rule_words.paper_environments_definition: The number of definition environments in the TeX source of each current paper, added up over the papers. These are counted separately from the statements the atlas lists for each paper.
rule_words.paper_environments_remark: The number of remark environments in the TeX source of each current paper, added up over the papers. These are counted separately from the statements the atlas lists for each paper.
rule_words.paper_environments_hypothesis: The number of hypothesis environments in the TeX source of each current paper, added up over the papers. These are counted separately from the statements the atlas lists for each paper.
rule_words.paper_environments_claim: The number of claim environments in the TeX source of each current paper, added up over the papers. These are counted separately from the statements the atlas lists for each paper.
rule_words.paper_environments_question: The number of question environments in the TeX source of each current paper, added up over the papers. These are counted separately from the statements the atlas lists for each paper.
rule_words.scope_class_headline: Each Lean statement an AI agent’s draft classifies as stating a paper’s theorem as the paper does. Nobody has reviewed the draft.
rule_words.scope_class_headline-part: Each Lean statement an AI agent’s draft classifies as stating part of a paper’s theorem. Nobody has reviewed the draft.
rule_words.scope_class_consequence: Each Lean statement an AI agent’s draft classifies as stating a consequence of a paper’s theorem. Nobody has reviewed the draft.
rule_words.scope_class_weaker: Each Lean statement an AI agent’s draft classifies as stating a weaker form of a paper’s theorem. Nobody has reviewed the draft.
rule_words.scope_class_supporting: Each Lean statement an AI agent’s draft classifies as stating a supporting result. Nobody has reviewed the draft.
rule_words.scope_class_unclear: Each Lean statement an AI agent’s draft classifies as unclear from OpenAI’s note. Nobody has reviewed the draft.
rule_words.scope_families_no_full_headline: Each family in which an AI agent’s draft finds no Lean statement that states a paper’s theorem as the paper does. The draft keeps its own date and has not been reviewed.
rule_words.scope_families_partial_headline_only: Each family in which an AI agent’s draft finds Lean statements of part of a paper’s theorem and none of a whole one. The draft keeps its own date and has not been reviewed.
rule_words.scope_families_with_lean_but_no_headline: Each family in which an AI agent’s draft finds Lean, but no statement of a paper’s theorem, whole or in part. The draft keeps its own date and has not been reviewed.
rule_words.scope_families_mixed_classes: Each family in which an AI agent’s draft puts the family’s Lean statements in more than one class. The draft keeps its own date and has not been reviewed.

about.title: About the atlas
about.what: The Plectis Atlas is an independent guide to OpenAI’s mathematics release of {release_date}. OpenAI groups related papers into {families} families. Of those, {families_with_lean} have statements written in Lean, software for writing mathematical statements and verifying proofs. Atlas provides reading pages for the papers, places Lean statements beside possible paper counterparts, and links independent assessments and proof-verification reports.
about.approach_intro: These essays shaped how the Atlas approaches explanation, credit and formal statements. Their authors are cited for their ideas; this does not imply endorsement or review of the Atlas.
about.approach_response_intro: What the atlas does in response:
approach_responses: Each family page quotes OpenAI’s description of its result and links the paper statements that may express it. Every paper has a reading page.
Where the release includes a Lean statement, Atlas places it beside a possible paper counterpart and reports independent assessments of what it expresses.
Atlas names the groups that examined statements or ran proof-verification programs and describes what their reports establish.
Each paper’s references are listed. Earlier work can be credited at the relevant passage, and independent reports retain their authors, dates and sources.
Contributors can explain results, compare statements or propose corrections, with named credit and disclosed AI assistance.

approach_items.title: The technical debt of AI-generated mathematics
approach_items.argues: argues that a correct result nobody can follow leaves a debt for other mathematicians to pay, and that whoever publicises such work should make it understandable.

approach_items.who: Silvia De Toffoli and Eamon Duede
approach_items.title: After Math
approach_items.argues: separate a valid answer, which a formal certificate can establish, from an intelligible solution that mathematicians can grasp, communicate and build on.

approach_items.title: Deep theorems were scarce and difficult
approach_items.argues: argues that theorem counts no longer show understanding, and asks that discovery, proof, formalisation and explanation each be credited.

approach_items.title: If math is more than proof
approach_items.argues: asks that motivated explanations, which show why a result is true and why it was worth asking, earn the credit that proofs do.

approach_items.who: A declaration posted by Terence Tao and first signed by 25 Fields Medallists
approach_items.title: A Severe Misalignment of AI in mathematics
approach_items.argues: warns that rushing AI systems at famous problems puts attribution and the human transmission of ideas at risk.

approach_items.title: A beginning for mathematics
approach_items.argues: argues that mathematics should be judged by human understanding, which makes the people who explain and teach it more necessary.

about.adds_heading: What the atlas adds to the release
about.adds_intro: OpenAI publishes {manuscripts} current papers as PDF and TeX, the typesetting source; {lean} Lean statement files for its Comparator proof-verification program; a catalogue; and notes on what the Lean statements express. For each of its {families} families, Atlas adds:
adds_items: a reading page for every paper, with links to individual theorems; incomplete conversions list what is missing, and the PDF remains the reference;
possible main theorems selected from shared wording, with links to their passages;
Lean statements beside possible paper counterparts, with the reason for each link and whether a comparison has been reviewed;
independent groups’ reports of running proof-verification programs on OpenAI’s proofs, credited and dated;
independent assessments of whether a family’s Lean statements express the result OpenAI describes in its catalogue, quoted in each group’s own terms;
reports of proofs in another proof assistant and exact calculations for finite claims;
citations between the release’s papers, with links in both directions;
forms for contributing an explanation, comparing statements or proposing a correction, with named credit.
about.backend: Statement Map, a program by Will Cook, collects the release’s statements, Lean files, independent assessments and contributions into versioned records. Atlas imports these records and computes possible paper matches from shared wording. Those matches are labelled as candidates; they are not reviews of mathematical meaning.
about.backend_pin: The imported records have generation identifier {generation}, format version {schema}, and exporter {exporter} from Statement Map revision {commit}. Validation report {receipt} records software tests at revision {runtime}. The site build rejects records that do not match this export’s version and file hashes. These tests validate the data format and consistency, not the mathematics.
about.backend_numbers: What each number counts, with its source records
about.independence_groups: It is equally independent of every group whose work it credits: {groups}. Each group’s findings are shown as their own, in their own terms, and none of them has reviewed or endorsed the atlas.
about.since_intro: Three pieces published since the release bear on how the atlas words what it shows.

since_items.title: What mathematicians should know about the Lean Theorem Prover: questions of reliability and AI
since_items.says: a guest post on Terence Tao’s blog (9 October 2026), explains that Lean’s kernel check is the core safeguard, and that a person must still confirm that a formal statement and its definitions say what was intended. This is why every Lean statement here is shown whole, with who compared it with the paper and what they found.

since_items.title: Changes to the Erdős problems web site
since_items.says: a guest post on Terence Tao’s blog (6 October 2026), describes removing problem statuses and the count of solved problems from erdosproblems.com, in favour of neutral wording such as “it is known that”, with a source. The atlas follows the same discipline: it says what is recorded and by whom, and keeps no tally of results.

since_items.title: AHM Statement on OpenAI’s October 6 Release of Mathematical Documents
since_items.says: reposted on Terence Tao’s blog (7 October 2026), sets out its view of the release and asks mathematicians to stop working with OpenAI. The atlas records it as one perspective on the release, and neither joins nor answers it.

about.since_note: None of these authors has reviewed or endorsed the atlas.
about.how: Scripts read release version {commit_short} and extract catalogue entries, paper sources, bibliographies, Lean statements and OpenAI’s notes. Each generated page links to its sources. Paper reading pages are converted from TeX. KaTeX tests whether the formulas can be typeset, not whether they are mathematically correct. Incomplete conversions list what is missing; the PDF remains the reference. Contribution status comes from Atlas’s own records.
about.independence: Atlas is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenAI. It describes the release, quotes OpenAI’s claims and links reports about specific statements, proofs and calculations.
about.licence: Original Atlas code and documentation use Apache-2.0; contributed explanations use CC BY 4.0. Imported source material, KaTeX and font subsets retain their own terms. The website includes their notices and licence texts.
about.cite: Use the citation below for the Atlas, with its revision or your access date. Also cite the original paper or outside report when relying on its result; a citation to the Atlas does not replace that credit.
about.author: {author} builds and maintains the atlas. His own work on Erdős problems, with its Lean proofs, is at Plectis.
about.made: Will Cook built Atlas with AI coding agents under his direction. The repository contains the scripts that extract and count material from the recorded release version. AI-drafted assessments of what the Lean statements express are labelled as drafts with no recorded human review. Named comparisons with papers and reports of proof verification are recorded separately.
about.not: Atlas records source material, assessments and reports of proof verification. It does not provide peer review or endorse the release’s results. Each page names the reports it records and the claims those reports cover.

sources.title: Sources

sources.credit: Atlas credits reports where they appear and links their sources. Original material retains its authorship and terms. A group’s proof-verification report, a statement extracted automatically from a paper, and a reviewed mathematical claim establish different facts; the page identifies which is being shown.
sources.openai_uses: The catalogue, the {manuscripts} current papers in {families} families with their TeX sources and bibliographies, the {lean} Lean statements and the Lean library, OpenAI’s Lean notes and its history file.

The method follows Will Cook’s claim-faithful publication system for his Erdős problem corpus.
